title: Wavelength and frequency
idea: All radio waves travel at the speed of light, so the higher the frequency, the shorter each wave, and the shorter the antenna.

lines: Wavelength in meters equals 300 divided by the frequency in megahertz
Speed of every radio wave in free space: the speed of light, 300,000,000 meters per second
Higher frequency = shorter wavelength = shorter antenna

compare.how: Shorter wavelength. Shorten an antenna and its resonant frequency goes up.
Longer wavelength. Lengthen an antenna and its resonant frequency goes down.

traps.wrong: Wavelength gets longer as frequency increases
traps.why: Backwards. More waves per second means each wave is shorter.

traps.wrong: Wavelength in meters equals frequency in megahertz divided by 300
traps.why: Upside down. 300 goes on top: 300 / 146 MHz = about 2 m.
Right number, wrong unit. It is 300,000,000 meters per second.
Frequency does not change the speed. All radio frequencies travel at the speed of light.
A longer antenna fits a longer wave, which is a lower frequency. Shortening it raises the frequency.
A half wave on 2 meters is about 38 inches. 19 inches is a quarter wave.
